item.title: Determinants, Permutations, Oh My!
item.description:
Matrix determinants have always been a rather mysterious math concept to me.

I think, like many students, I first encountered determinants in my undergraduate linear algebra class. Our textbook1 gave the Laplace expansion method of computing determinants as the definition of determinants, making them seem like an abstract property of square matrices which just so happens to be useful in subsequent theorems like the fact that a square matrix is invertible if and only if . Only later did I learn about the relationship between determinants and the volume of parallelotopes formed from the columns of square matrices, developing some much-needed geometric intuition.

1 D. Lay, S. Lay and J. McDonald. Linear Algebra and its Applications, 5th ed. Pearson Education, 2016.

2 The Princeton Review. Cracking the GRE Mathematics Subject Test, 4th ed. Random House, 2010.

However, while studying for the GRE Math Subject Test,2 I stumbled across a fascinating formula for computing determinants involving permutations which I had never seen before.

Welcome to my blog!

Here, I plan to write about a variety of topics that interest me: math, data science, software development, art, and so on. I will try my best to assign categories to my blog posts so you (the dear reader) can filter them by what interests you.
